judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns entirely on defined terms — "ultimate net loss," "retained limit," "occurrence" — and the phrase "to which this policy applies" imports every exclusion and endorsement, so its reach is not self-contained and "legally obligated to pay as damages" is itself contestable (does it include defense outlay?).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Definition c (which excludes loss and legal expenses from ultimate net loss) and Insuring Agreement II (supplementary payments only where underlying insurance does not apply), the scope of what this promise actually indemnifies is genuinely in play.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Covered by underlying insurance" is ambiguous between expenses of a type the underlying policy insures and expenses the underlying insurer actually pays or has limits left to pay, and it is a single general phrase carrying the whole exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against the II lead-in (payments only where the loss is "not covered" by underlying insurance) and II(b) (company assumes defense on exhaustion of underlying limits), leaving the umbrella's defense-cost obligation after exhaustion genuinely unresolved.
judgments.clause_name: Insuring Agreement II(a) — underlying insurance defense/legal expense exclusion (Umbrella Policy)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause excludes "all loss expenses and legal expenses (including attorneys' fees, court costs and interest)" but the trailing words "and all salaries of employees and office expenses of the insured; the company or any underlying insurer so incurred" are punctuated so as to leave whose expenses are meant unclear — a mechanical defect on top of a scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against Insuring Agreement II(c) ("pay all expenses incurred by the company, all costs taxed against the insured and all interest") and Condition 4 (taxable costs and interest payable in addition to the limit), so whether legal expenses are ever indemnified is contestable across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/reliance preamble; nothing in it operates on coverage and no term needs construing beyond the declarations it references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Declarations and the Wisconsin Declarations amendatory endorsement on misrepresentation; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The qualifier "not covered by any underlying coverage ... or any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured" repeats the same "covered" ambiguity, though as a lead-in its work is limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be harmonised with the same section's later paragraphs (a) and (b) governing occurrences where underlying insurance does apply, which is where the friction actually lies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Defend any suit ... even if groundless, false or fraudulent" is conventional language, but the tail permitting settlement "as it deems expedient" leaves the company's discretion loosely bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Asbestos endorsement's express no-duty-to-defend and against II(a) on underlying-covered defense; the duty is conditioned rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bond-premium obligations are enumerated with a clear disclaimer of any duty to furnish bonds; wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Condition 4 (Appeals) and the limit provisions; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All expenses incurred by the company" and post-judgment interest are stated with a clear cap by reference to the company's limit; the wording itself is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against Definition c's exclusion of legal expenses and interest from ultimate net loss, though the "in addition to ultimate net loss" sentence is designed to reconcile them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable expenses, other than loss of earnings, incurred at the company's request" is a narrow and familiar formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the rest of the supplementary payments section and Condition 3's cooperation duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Immediately in excess of underlying insurance listed on the declarations page without intervening insurance" is a condition whose application to a partially exhausted or unlisted layer is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Condition 9 (Other Insurance), Condition 13 (maintenance of underlying insurance) and paragraph (a) above it, so the trigger for assuming defense is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out "except settlement of claims or suits" is terse and its interaction with the listed payments is not obvious on the face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Definition c and II(c), it is the reconciling sentence, and its adequacy for that job is itself arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A savings clause for jurisdictions where the company cannot carry out the agreement; the operative promise (pay expenses incurred with written consent) is clear enough.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; no operative content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Errors or omissions, malpractice or mistake of a professional nature ... as a collection agency" is bounded by the business activity named.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three-limb trigger is precise, but the drop-down operates over "underlying insurance listed in this policy and identified as being listed for contingency coverage purposes," a description whose referent is not stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Appropriate premium charge" at the company's "sole option" is loose, but it is a familiar pricing mechanic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends the territory provisions of a "Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy," but no such coverage part is attached to this umbrella form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Legal or other expenses necessarily incurred" is a soft measure, and the indemnity is conditioned on the loss being determined payable under this policy — arguably self-cancelling in a genuine priority fight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanism is arithmetically clear (one-third of a trebled award), though the label "exclusion" for a partial payment obligation is loose.
